A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
L-trytophan injection in rats inhibits the activity of the enzymes involved in the metabolism of L-alanine and L-glutamate, the main amino acids of the alanine cycle.
L-trytophan injection in fasted rats results in a marked inhibition of extramitochondial L-alanine- and L-aspartate-2-ketoglutamate aminotransfersase.

L-trytophan injection inhibits the activity of the enzymes of the L-alanine cycle in the cytosol and the activity of GDH in the mitochondria of the liver of fast rats, whereas in the fed rats, L-tryptphan injection does not affect these activities.
